title: What happens when we add up odd numbers?
description: The odd numbers are added from the start, one at a time. The totals are one, four, nine, sixteen, twenty five and thirty six, and Keeko's doubt, that the totals go up by the same amount each time, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: adding the odd numbers from the start gives the square numbers one after another. Watch for students who expect the totals to grow by a fixed amount.

source: What happens when we start adding up odd numbers? 1 = 1; 1 +
video_script.why: The child adds the odd numbers from the start, writes each total, and sees that the totals are the square numbers.
video_script.substitution: Keep adding the next odd number and write down every total.
video_script.anchor: a growing line of sums: one, one plus three, one plus three plus five, and so on, each with its total beside it
video_script.wrong_answer: the totals go up by the same amount each time
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the totals go up by the same amount each time. The totals are one, four, nine and sixteen, which go up by three, five and seven, so the jumps keep growing, and the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The sums are the square numbers

final_answer.value: The sums are the square numbers 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, ...
final_answer.spoken: the sums are the square numbers

hold_back: The sums are the square numbers
never_show: the totals go up by the same amount each time
maths_rules: the totals 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36 are the square numbers
slip: the totals go up by 3, 5, 7, so the jumps are not the same
video_script.design: One idea: add the odd numbers from the start and the totals are squares. Assumes square numbers are known as 1, 4, 9, 16. Wrong idea: the totals go up by the same amount. The list of sums stays on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the odd numbers 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 in a row, with a plus sign between them and an empty box for each total

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.odd: the odd numbers one, three, five, seven, nine and eleven appear in a row
marks.ask: the words what happens appear over the row

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about adding odd numbers.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>We start with one, then add three, then five, and so on.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What happens to the total as we keep adding?

beats.on_screen: the row of odd numbers holds still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one counter, then three more counters added to make a new total, then five more

marks.add: one counter appears and three more counters join it
marks.total: the new total is written beside the counters

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Adding puts amounts together into one total.
<bookmark mark='total'/>We add the odd numbers from the start, and after each one we stop and write the total.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the odd numbers one, three, five, seven, nine and eleven.

beats.on_screen: To find: what the totals are

marks.find: the words what the totals are are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find what the totals are as we add one odd number at a time.

marks.four: the line 1 + 3 = 4 is written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, the first two totals. One by itself is one.
<bookmark mark='four'/>One plus three is four, so the second total is four.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Step two, add the next odd numbers. One plus three plus five is nine.
<bookmark mark='sixteen'/>One plus three plus five plus seven is sixteen, which is the fourth total.

marks.twenty: the line with total 25 is written
marks.thirty: the line with total 36 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='twenty'/>Step three, keep going. Adding nine gives a total of twenty five.
<bookmark mark='thirty'/>Adding eleven as well gives a total of thirty six for six odd numbers.

marks.list: the six totals are circled in a column and read from top to bottom

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step four, look at the totals. They are one, four, nine, sixteen, twenty five and thirty six. We know these numbers from before.

beats.on_screen: Answer: The sums are the square numbers
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The sums are the square numbers.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble; the totals 1, 4, 9, 16 in a row with the gaps 3, 5, 7 written between them; the bubble is struck through

marks.gaps: the gaps between the totals are written, three, five and seven

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the totals go up by the same amount each time.
<bookmark mark='gaps'/>But the totals one, four, nine and sixteen go up by three, then five, then seven.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The jumps keep growing, because each new odd number is bigger than the last.
